title: streaming-lifecycle-controls-client-cancel-disconnect-reconnect-timeouts
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: customer-facing issues and internal load tests exposed several streaming lifecycle edgecases: 1) client-initiated cancels over HTTP/1.1 and websockets were not always honored by the server when requests were de-duplicated or routed through proxies; 2) disconnects could leave partial in-flight state and KV cache pins, causing resource leakage and out-of-order resume attempts; 3) reconnect/resume semantics across the OpenAI-compatible streaming layer were underspecified (no resume token or partial event reconciliation), leading to duplicated tool/function calls after flaky mobile network reconnects; 4) server-side idle/request timeouts were conservative and either aborted healthy resumable streams or left long-lived goroutines. Changes: this PR implements a cohesive set of streaming lifecycle controls: - explicit client-cancel propagation and idempotent cancel handling across router and worker layers; - connection-disconnect cleanup that releases KV cache pins and cancels downstream inference subrequests; - resume token support in the OpenAI-compatible streaming protocol: server emits a resume_token event (opaque string) at consistent checkpoints and clients can request resume using ?resume_token=<token>; - guarded resume semantics to reconcile already-delivered events and avoid re-invoking tool/function calls by tracking event checkpoints per-stream; - server-side adaptive timeouts: short tail timeout for failed handshakes, idle stream GC with exponential backoff per-customer, and stronger eviction for stuck KV contexts; - end-to-end test coverage in runtime/integration tests, added unit tests for router cancellation, and updated python/typescript compatibility examples. Backwards compatibility: resume_token is additive to the OpenAI-compatible stream event types and is ignored by older clients; cancel semantics are idempotent and will not change previously committed side effects. Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default (runtime.streaming.lifecycle_controls) for 2 weeks in canary, then enabled for all hosted nodes after monitoring verification. Checklist: - [x] implement cancel propagation (router + worker) - [x] add disconnect cleanup and KV pin release - [x] add resume_token event and resume endpoint handling - [x] prevent duplicate tool/function invocation on resume - [x] add adaptive server timeouts and GC - [x] tests (unit + integration) - [x] docs and examples updated - [x] canary rollout plan added

release_notes: Streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel propagation, disconnect cleanup, resume_token-based reconnect/resume for OpenAI-compatible streams, adaptive server timeouts and KV pin eviction. Backwards-compatible and feature-flagged; rollout planned to canary for 2 weeks.
notes: Observability: added metrics runtime.streaming.resume_attempts, runtime.streaming.resume_success, runtime.streaming.duplicate_tool_invocations; dashboards and alerts will be onboarded during canary. Monitoring owner: @sre-streaming.
example_usage: Modern clients: on network drop, re-open websocket with ?resume_token=<token>. Server will emit resume events up to last checkpoint and then continue streaming. SDK examples updated in python and typescript.
